case_title: Ranjeet Singh @ Dara v. State of Madhya Pradesh
neutral_facts: The accused, a stepson of the deceased, was found in the room where the deceased was found dead with incised wounds. His clothes were blood-stained, and he was holding a blood-stained sword in his hand. The deceased was the stepmother of the accused and lived with her son, who was the son of the deceased's husband. The accused was a regular visitor to the house of the deceased's brother. On the day of the incident, the accused arrived from Bhopal and parked his car outside the house. The deceased was found dead in the room, and the accused was found holding a sword with blood-stained hands. The police arrived, and the accused opened the door, admitting to the murder. The post-mortem report indicated that the deceased had incised wounds consistent with a sharp-edged weapon like a sword. The accused failed to explain his presence in the room or the presence of the blood-stained sword. The courts below concluded that the circumstances pointed to the accused's guilt.
